La Nuit Trésor à la Folie by Lancôme is a Oriental Vanilla fragrance for women. La Nuit Trésor à la Folie was launched in 2018. La Nuit Trésor à la Folie was created by Christophe Raynaud, Amandine Clerc-Marie and Honorine Blanc. Top notes are Red Currant, Pink Pepper, Pear and Bergamot; middle notes are Damask Rose, Violet, Peony and Jasmine; base notes are Bourbon Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Benzoin, Nutmeg, Ambroxan, Patchouli and Woody Notes.

Lancôme fragrance collection of LA NUIT TRÉSOR expands with another edition in early 2018 called La Nuit Trésor à la Folie. Imagined to be a rose garden, the line features Rose Aphrodisiaque in the original La Nuit Trésor Eau de Parfum, Rose Caresse in the eponymous Eau de Parfum and Rose Passion is in La Nuit Trésor Eau de Toilette. The new flower is Rose Fougueuse, the heroine of La Nuit Trésor à la Folie flanker.

La Nuit Trésor à la Folie is Lancôme's interpretation of love in the form of letting go and surrendering. The composition is developed by perfumers Christophe Raynaud, Amandine Marie and Honorine Blanc.

Top notes: pink pepper, bergamot, pear, red currant

Heart: Damask rose, jasmine, peony, violet

Base: Bourbon vanilla, benzoin, tonka, patchouli, woody notes, ambroxan, nutmeg

Available as a 30, 50 and 75 ml Eau de Parfum.

MademoiselleMaya 09/25/25 08:52

The best La Nuit Trésor flanker until Le Parfum.
This is much lighter than the pillar or Le Parfum.
Can be worn during a day and night in colder weather though I do not rule out spring and even summer evening.
Complex scent. The notes are all in low volume creating a new quality.
In the opening I feel red currants, nutmeg, bergamot and the tonka beans of the base. I feel floral notes, too, but which flower I do not know - they are blended to perfection. The rose here is lipsticky.
Soft, alluring, lovely.
Fruits well blended with flowers and the warmth of the base which is surprisingly light for a La Nuit Trésor. I feel mainly tonka and vanilla.
À La Folie is a departure from the pillar.
If you miss it - check Mon Guerlain Intense out. It also has the mysterious mix of vanilla-tonka as the main story.
During wear it also becomes similar to Lady Castagnette by Lulu Castagnette which is a bit more fruity.
The dry-down is amazing. Like a gentler and less girly Flowerbomb. Sweet, floral and multifaceted. It appears at 5 hours mark.
The scent lasts very well, applied at 6p.m it lingers till the morning with its similarities to Flowerbomb Nectar's dry-down.

Maya lilac 04/04/24 06:46

Tresor La Nuit a la Folie is another example of the best scent in the line that gets discontinued. Why, nobody knows…

As a lover of original Tresor, I have sampled through years all the flankers released. This, A la Folie, and the summery one, Nude, were my favourites. Discontinued both now!

A la Folie is the most addictive, sweet, leaning gourmand of the line. Has a considerable amount of vanilla, tonka beans and benzoin mixed with some fruits, some spices, some flowers, some woods and patchouli leaves. The results of these beautiful blended notes was a scrumptious, delicious, mouthwatering rich vanilla scent with gourmand, powdery touches!

Performance was great, like most of Lancome’s perfumes, A la Folie lasts well and has moderate sillage. I always appreciate a good lasting perfume and Lancome rarely disappoints.

I don’t understand the logic of discontinuing A la Folie, when it was the most popular in the Tresor line! I see that’s the general sentiment in the comments section here, not just me thinking that. People seem to miss A la Folie, so I doubt Lancome did discontinued it because it wouldn’t sell well..

And personal opinion now, I think nowadays Tresor line is more loved than La Vie est Belle line. Sometimes these designers brands don’t seem to make sense with their decisions to axe the more popular ones from their catalog! I rest my case.

You’ll be greatly missed when I am done with my bottle..

Shanty36 01/12/24 09:07

I blind bought this because (1) i really like the la nuit tresor line and (2) it was raved about as the best flanker on YT to no end, so when i saw it pop up on an online retailer I SNATCHED it up because i cant find it anywhere. Is it nice? Yes. Do i regret buying it? No. But it's not my favourite flanker (that top spot so far goes to the intense flanker, which they also discontinued...).

This version to me has the most body of the flankers ive tried. The base notes are creamier, and come across caramel-like to me (i think it's the tonka bean mixing with the nutmeg to give me that effect). The sweetness is also better enveloped in the blend of notes here, so i can definitely see why people liked this one so much. The other flankers i think focus more around the fruity notes as the star of the show if you will, versus a more balanced blend in this one. If you like the la nuit tresor line i would definitely recommend checking it out if you can find it and if you like a slightly more gourmand style.

yukikiki 12/22/23 15:23

One of my favorites. It's a blend of vanilla, fruits, and some woods to tone the sweetness down. When I first smelled it, it was like a very flavorful rich vanilla-fruit frosting. It's got a dark, sultry element to it that makes it great for date nights. I wouldn't say any notes stand out too much. It's all very well blended together. I will say though that I don't really detect peony, bergamot, or patchouli. The fragrance is just so good and it gets better as it dries down, as the vanilla, woods, and fruit start to blend more and more together. The nutmeg gives it a mouth watering quality without making the fragrance smell dry or sharp.

It's quite long lasting and has quite a bit of projection. It's one of the few fragrances where I can't overspray - I usually do 10+. But with this fragrance it's half that and if I spray more, I get a headache. For me that's good, especially since it's been discontinued and I only have two 30ml backup bottles. I don't know why Lancome had to discontinue such a gem. At the moment, the Lancome site doesn't have it.

rene.saller 12/11/23 17:31

A rich and gourmandy rose scent--it smells chocolatey to me, but cocoa isn't listed as a note, so I'm probably just smelling the vanilla mixed with the berries and other accords. I also discern something that reminds me very much of a purple bearded iris, but again, that could be the violet-peony-jasmine cocktail. I like La Nuit Trésor à la Folie quite a bit, but I probably won't buy a full bottle once my 0.27-ounce purse-spray runs out. It's close enough to some other dessert rose fragrances in my collection--including a recent cheapie that I love, Mohra Silky Rose, by Lattafa--that I don't really need it. I could always wear La Vie est Belle Iris Absolu or Shalimar Millésime Tonka or Vanille Orchidée or Dior Addict if I'm going to wear a floral gourmand. That's not to say La Nuit Trésor à la Folie isn't the equal of those perfumes, only that I already have more perfumes than I can reasonably wear, so I might as well put a moratorium on buying any more--at least until I deplete a few bottles, and that might take years. I'd also like to pare down my scent library to fragrances that I love unreservedly (not merely like).

natasha28 09/14/23 00:06

Tresor la nuit a la folie - I'm glad I only bought the smaller 8ml sample. The box was outside when it was -14c out with the wind chill. The perfumes were cold, but it didn't freeze, I don't know if that would make a difference. On the first spray, it has a very strong alcohol scent. You can kind of get a hint of the pear- reminds me a tiny bit of JLo Live. Also a slight pink pepper note, not as strong as Miss Dior Absolutely Blooming though, similar opening but la folie dried down more powder and light, while Absol.Blooming is strong. It's sweet but not really the comforting sweet I usually like. That part fades after about 5 minutes.  It smells like it would fit into the Tresor flankers (but I wouldn't think Tresor if I didn't know it was part of the line), it's a LOT lighter than I thought it'd be! I think it's spicer than La Nuit OG, but not as gourmand as OG.  It sits close to the skin, maybe in the summer it'd be stronger, but the notes are more fall/winter daytime in a cozy sweater. It smells a bit spicy and sweet. Very subtle baby powder note when I sniff it rapidly, floral rose and sweet. I can't detect the pink pepper specifically, but there is some spiciness. I can't detect the patchouli, which is great! The OG La Nuit has a moderate amount of patchouli that makes it very strong, but still wearable for me (not like Britney Spears Fantasy Intense). There aren't any coconut notes listed, but I get a similar vibe.
The more I smell it the more I like it. After about an hour the powder notes are really nice! It's like an innocent soft comforting pretty powdery version of La Nuit. It'd be a nice daytime scent for women 20/30-45 years old. I wonder if it might smell nice on a man too? It's a bit too femme to be strictly male though.
I don't know if I would keep it if gifted, I might it's just so light. If it was a scent bomb like Tresor La Nuit I'd keep it. The price is too high for the lack of silage. Edit: The longer I wear it the more it's starting to grow on me!

Strawberrykitty 08/29/23 11:42

This is my favorite perfume that I don’t actually wear. I like to spray it on a stuffed animal bunny and fall asleep, inhaling the sweet vapors of nostalgia. This was a blind buy because I liked other scents from Lancôme, and ended up smelling like my late maternal grandmother’s house. She passed when I was 11 and I was absolutely shocked when I realized what I was smelling. Though, this doesn’t smell “grandma-ish,” and I resent the usage of that phrase and similar ageist phrases to describe fragrance. Just say that it isn’t to your taste and move on.

This is a powdery amber vanilla scent that is sweet but not Pink Sugar sweet. Just right imo. The rose isn’t that prominent to me, and you can definitely smell the fruity touch from the pear and black currant. I think this is “well blended” in the sense that you can’t smell a harsh transition from opening to the drydown. I’m pretty sure my grandma’s house smelled like this because of an airfreshener spray like Febreeze or her decorative potpourri and candles, but I think this would be good for night time or date nights for those that haven’t been to my grandma’s house; we all have scent associations and this happens to be mine, and that’s ok. I’ve never smelled that specific scent again, despite being in many houses with older people and potpourri over the years, so I don’t think that it was the result commercially available scented products.

I was heartbroken when my grandma passed away. She lived in a different state than us, so my family would always travel to her and my grandpa’s house in the summer. My uncles had built a swing between two big trees in their backyard, and I remember running to the swing as soon as I got to their house. I’d then go through the kitchen door into the house and find my grandma making food or downstairs in her reclining chair. I’d sit on her lap while she watched the wheel of fortune with my grandpa, eating cashews that my grandpa offered me. They’re both gone now and I wish that I had longer with them. I only spray this when I want to think of them, so I have worn this once at night going out. I mostly spray this on the bunny before going to bed and hope that I dream of them.

This seems to react differently on my skin than on most. The main notes of vanilla and rose are blatantly there but the woody base is strong and is really what drives this fragrance on me. The wood is a light, vanilla wood at its core but the pepper and spice notes merge with it and give it a bit of darkness and depth which prevent a pencil shaving effect from happening.

Let me take a step back and reiterate here, the woodiness does not merely drive this fragrance on my skin but absolutely dominates. It is a feminine woodiness but it is STRONG.

The rose is deep and sensual and soft and velvety. The phrase “gentle red” comes to mind.

This is not a gourmand by any means on my skin and is definitely not sexy on me either but it is very elegant and is romantic in a maternal sort of way. A warm, securing embrace by a large and fancy lady who is sweet and soft but also strong and supportive.

*loves_shoes* 04/05/22 05:32

BUY THIS LIMITED EDITION FLANKER WHILE YOU CAN!

I blind bought 30ml based on reviews, just to see what the hype was about.
And it’s really good.
A stunning warm, fruity, vanilla.
The florals are not identifiable, they just give complexity and roundness to the fragrance.
As it dries, it develops a delicious soft spicy richness, you can smell a lot of benzoin on the skin (nose to skin!), it has a slightly medicinal edge to it. But all that projects is a warm, sweet yet spicy, amber vanilla. It has a lovely depth to it that is often missing from most fruity florals I try.

I own that tropical looking skull (Police to be exotic jungle) and it smells NOTHING like this to my nose. Exotic jungle is a plain vanilla fruity floral and has NONE of the delicious softly spicy benzoin and tonka in this.

A la folie is wonderful and I wish I’d bought a bigger bottle.

Edit: I should say that I can’t really smell ambroxan properly, but this is still lovely as there’s plenty else her to smell. And maybe the ambroxan is what makes it project so well and last so long.

Edit 2: same day, 9 hours later and I just bought 2 back up bottles. It’s that good.

Edit 3: Directly compared to the original La Nuit using testers still available in the airport. A La Folie projected more, and lasted longer (it lasted through an 18 hour 2 flight trip, and was still present as a skin scent when I was trying to test new things in our final destination!).

I got out my bottle of Parfait de Roses to be curious and it smells a bit like the DNA of Parfait de Roses without the powdery sugar but with more added vanilla. Lancome has a distinct rose accord they use that is always familiar in their rose based fragrances which I love. I feel more comfortable spraying this one more because the others are discontinued and are very expensive and special. This is a well blended bourbon vanilla like you smell in Dior Addict and it's mixed with red currant, rose with some spice from the nutmeg but its not overly spicy..definately has tonka to sweeten it up...it's so well blended and sweet and feels a bit creamy because of the bourbon vanilla. I am so happy I got this fragrance. A la Folie lasts and it's dense and the scent cloud envelopes you. The vanilla is so good. Highly recommend this fragrance and the bottle in person is so gorgeous. And I have to agree with others it will grow on you as it develops over time.

I've come to really love Lancome fragrances for their quality. RavenValkyrie 07/31/21 21:32

La Nuit Trésor à la Folie is sacred to Gourmand-lovers for a reason.
A real Goddess of seduction.
She's elegant, lethal sensuality with an edible allure, nothing left to do but give in to the temptation and become a temptress yourself.

Save it for special occasions - not an every day type of scent.

I remember years ago smelling this fragrance for the first time, walking around in the airport in Amsterdam with my sister, wanting to kill some time like everyone else; entering the duty free shop and seeing this beauty on the shelf....
I tried it on my wrist.. And there I was : Instantly Hooked.
Needless to say: I immediately sprayed it on my sister as well.. She was Hooked too.
So we bought our first bottles of this weapon of mass seduction as the perfect souvenir-ending of our trip.
Then we left the shop, sat at some restaurant and ordered champagne and chocolate dipped strawberries to spend our last money before boarding the plane.. and I still recall the small whiffs of this fragrance that ensnared me whenever I held the glass to my lips or took a bite of the stawberry...The boozy, luscious vanilla, the creamy woodsy notes and the lovely, savory rose .... were more intoxicating than the champagne and just as insatiably appetizing as the strawberries.
.. and on the plane ride home we were feeling the effects as true devotees/addicts: I continuously had my nose fixated at my wrist and my sister was using the safety instruction card as a fan to better smell the perfume - because the rich, lush dry-down of this fragrance is Divine.
..
We knew then, what we still know now: La Nuit Trésor à la Folie will always be one of our most treasured and undying fragrance-obsessions

Abby Normal 07/04/21 01:51

Looking to see if I'd voted on this gem from my collection, I also see that I haven't reviewed it yet. And this is a favorite, let me tell you why.
I adore gourmand roses and this one is downright edible. The rich, opulent (and prominent) combination of vanilla/tonka bean/benzoin is intoxicating; the red currant inviting, ripe, and juicy; the rose wraps herself around through the accords like a velvet rope: rich but delicate and never too heavy, even to the point of being light-hearted (and herein is where I concur with the name choice, "a la Folie" as well).
The performance is better than moderate in every regard: she is a strong opener and performer with noticeable sillage and respectable lasting-power.
Given the perceived overall quality of La Nuit Tresor a la Folie, current asking prices are right on the money. 😏
The bottle/packaging is stunning; the 100ml bottle is still manageable by smaller, female hands for application without worry of dropping or mis-spraying accidents, too.
If you know that you enjoy gourmand roses, please give this one a trial run as you may find another true love.

I've been donning myself in this elixir over the past few days, and I have to be honest, it's surprisingly disappointing to me.
Don't get me wrong, this is Lancome and it smells luxe - however it is just straight forward Vanilla from start to finish and I was hoping for more - it is incredibly linear.
What my nose can pick out is a deep, rich vanilla enhanced by incredibly smooth benzoin, with some unidentified and intertwined notes. If you're a vanilla lover, there's NO chance that you won't like it.
Always gorgeous, can be ever so slightly cloying, large sillage and beastly longevity - overall it gets a 7/10 from me :)

EDIT: I do have to add, the more I wear this, the farther I fall for it. Personally, fragrance is a very special thing. I have quite a few in my collection and almost every single one of them is associated with a positive memory or feeling.
I've recently separated from my partner (RIP Prada Candy Florale) and it's given a new meaning to this perfume.
To me, this smells of strength and courage. Of hope and reassurance. I feel that Lancome, the masters that they are, have created something beyond beautiful. And honestly, I hope to read more of people and their stories.

Signature worthy. Love at first sniff.

The dry down is AMAZING! The opening is sweet and a little fruity (I'm usually not into fruity smells but it's) followed by delicate florals that are rounded by a vanilla drydown. I LOVE the amazing vanilla that this turns into after 30 minutes. WOW!

mychinarose 10/19/18 07:18

I think the big thing people want to know is: What is the difference between the original La Nuit Tresor and LNT a la Folie? (At least I did). To my nose, the simple difference comes down to this: chocolate vs. vanilla. Let me 'splain.

First of all, these are the notes that the two frags share: Pear & bergamot up top, rose in the middle (albeit "different" roses), patchouli, vanilla and some tonka at the bottom. This must be the LNT DNA because upon first spray of LNT-ALF I get a blast of familiarity of the former.

But then while LNT is more fruity and buttery, almost chocolate--to me this is from the praline-caramel-coffee-licorice combo (and what a decadent combo that is!)--ALF is, at it's heart, a true vanilla. I'm talking buttercream frosting white birthday cake vanilla. This is from the bourbon vanilla-tonka bean-benzoin explosion. At some point in the day, at least by hour 4 of wear, all previous notes seem to dissipate on me and this is just vanilla cupcake (reminds me a LOT of Laura Mercier Eau Gourmand Vanille).

I love it. YUM.

If you LOVE vanilla, and you love La Nuit Tresor, you should definitely own this. I love that a la Folie is very long lasting vanilla on me, which is pretty rare. By bedtime last night I could still smell it, and I sprayed conservatively in the morning.

I'm not sure at this point which version I like better, but I'm definitely happy that I have both.

terezzz 02/20/19 07:31

Oh my goodness... this perfume is just heaven! I get an image of eating creme brulée with red currant or some other vanilla dessert, and drinking red wine. The rose is also very prominent but it's more sweet and seductive rather than fresh and floral. I feel like the sweetness of the rose in this makes it more of a mature gourmand fragrance (I picture ages 20 and up) and not a pink sugar or viva la juicy type of sweetness.

La Nuit Tresor in comparison is more of a clubbing fragrance with a fruity and caramel character, while this one is more suitable for a romantic date with notes of red currant and vanilla. Personally I prefer A La Folie because it's more delicious and unique. I'd recommend it to someone who enjoys gourmands and scents like Midnight Rose, CH Good Girl and maybe even Black Opium. Longevity is good, I'd say about 8 hours! Can I also mention the beautiful bottle? The red is absolutely stunning and fits the scent perfectly! LOVE!

iamoir 01/25/18 14:16

My nose must be broken. The perfume pyramid presents an array of notes, just like in La nuit tresor, for a quite complex and deep smelling flanker that in no way contains only:
•rose essence
•bourbon vanilla
•patchouli essence
as the official site of Lancome states.

Nevertheless, I don't fully agree with the intensity of the notes shown up there. A la folie is definitely not as sweet as presented, at least in my opinion. In fact I thought it would be another gourmand as its sister, but here comes the surprise with a modernized balsamic perfume.

It has a soft rosey opening with fruity balmy nuances here and there. The fruit is really non-descript and the lytchee that prevails in the original, still makes an appearance here. The rose does get heavier and the final drydown consists of woods and incense.

More sour than sweet, so woody, very incensey-not the orthodox variety, that I can confirm-, heady and bit powdery. More original than La nuit tresor? Sure. And as heavy. A wintery nightime scent that die hard fans of La nuit tresor will need. Well blended and long lasting.

Sensual, adult-appropriate.
